newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures end up in continued slow trade.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures end up in continued slow trade.

text.p: Slow trade persisted in CME lumber futures and prices drifted higher on thin short covering, traders said.

The market continues to lack a definite direction and moved up slightly on its current discount to cash. But thin rolling of longs from May into July weighed on May. Gains were also limited by the continued slow cash trade and weak undertone to the spruce market, they said.
Lumber closed $0.50 to $4.00 per tbf higher with May up the least at $389.50 and July up most at $386.90 per tbf.
